validity_findings.finding: All measurements remain localhost Flask 3.1.3 + SQLite WAL + TTL 0.5s + jitter 10-100ms + HS256/RS256 JWT on 127.0.0.1:18951, seed 42, p_refresh_success=0.7, sequential client, threaded=False. No production OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, or database-backed sessions. Producer correctly bounds claim_ceiling to this substrate in result.json validity_notes #1 and report.md Claim Ceiling. No production or PRODUCT_CORE inference warranted.

Behavioral_score is discrete bimodal (0.35 failure / 0.65 success), not continuous severity variation. Recomputed from raw_evidence: phase_b 0.65=341/480, 0.35=139/480; phase_d 0.65=34/60, 0.35=26/60; noise-only exactly 0.05. Per-condition behavioral_std 0.1332-0.1411 and isolated 0.1499 are driven solely by Bernoulli p_refresh_success=0.7 mixing, not graded severity. Spec measurement_validity #2 explicitly defines this as expected (bimodal ~0.35/~0.65), so it is not a protocol violation, but it limits production severity generalization. Producer discloses this in validity_notes #2 (though it misstates failure mode as ~0.48 instead of observed 0.35).

Detection at threshold 0.25 is tautological given bimodal scores: both modes (0.35 and 0.65) exceed 0.25, so TP=1.0 for any threshold in [0.15,0.35]. Recomputed threshold_sensitivity confirms TP=1.0 at 0.15-0.35 (540/540) and cliff to 0.694 at 0.40 (375/540), FP=0.0 at all thresholds. The metric does not discriminatingly test noise robustness; it is guaranteed by scoring weights (failure: 0.30(401)+0.03(admin)+0.02(session_valid)=0.35). Producer correctly reports this as flat TP and states '0.25 not uniquely optimal' in validity_notes #5 and report.md Phase E. Exploratory per prereg #9, does not affect C2 decision.

NC-NOISE-FP FP=0.0 on 240 noise-only samples (60 per noise type) with behavioral_score exactly 0.05 in every sample (no variance). Deterministic scoring makes FP test low-power: any threshold 0.15-0.40 yields same FP=0.0. Recomputed FP=0/240=0.0 matches producer. Pass at <=0.15 is valid per frozen rule, but does not demonstrate calibrated false-positive control under stochastic scoring.

Producer narrative misstates failure-mode behavioral_score as ~0.48 in result.json validity_notes #2, report.md Detailed Findings (Token Refresh Variance, Phase E), and result.json observations 'ranges from ~0.48 to ~0.65'. Raw evidence recompute shows failure mode is 0.35 (not 0.48). Report also states 'Token_refresh behavioral score under noise (mean 0.55-0.57) is slightly lower than isolated (mean 0.52)' but isolated mean is 0.52 which is lower, not higher (inverted). Neither error affects numeric metrics or decision logic; numeric metrics in result.json.metrics are correct (behavioral_mean 0.552-0.57 vs isolated 0.52). Flagged for correction but not material to SURVIVES determination.

validity_findings.finding: N=480 paired samples satisfied (4 co-occurring conditions x 120), plus 240 noise-only, 60 isolated, 48 threshold probes = 868 HTTP cycles. Server state reset via set_drift(None) between conditions correctly implemented; no cross-condition contamination observed (per-condition score ranges consistent, cache_status distribution credible). RNG seeded 42 before server thread start, server threaded=False, client sequential - reproducible. Frozen measurement_validity N>=480 satisfied, resolving parent V1 (N=240) violation.

No behavioral-structural leakage: behavioral_signal from /api/session/status (body status/new_token_issued/role/status_code), structural_signal from /api/schema (cardinality of body keys + header count). Structural noise (optional_field_addition etc.) affects only /api/schema, drift affects only /api/session/status. Orthogonality recomputed correctly.
